summary: The starter prompt clearly defines the goal (a Python LangChain agent that uses a DocumentDB aggregation tool to find care gaps, injects guidelines, prioritises patients, and writes outreach talking points). It omits many engineering details (Python version, driver/version, exact data model, model/provider, indexes, app surface, infra, tests). The skill.md run environment supplies the live cluster details and the DATABASE name and the DOCUMENTDB_URI env var, but no 'DocumentDB skill' is actually installed. A builder can start, but will make a number of concrete assumptions (Python 3.10+, PyMongo driver, collections named 'patients' etc., a CLI demo script, OpenAI-compatible LLM) unless the author specifies otherwise.

rubric.found_in_prompt: identify patients missing recommended screenings based on age, diagnosis, and last-visit documents; prioritise the patient list and generate outreach talking points
rubric.note: Business problem and what the sample demonstrates are stated.

rubric.found_in_prompt: build a Python LangChain agent with a DocumentDB aggregation tool

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Target Python 3.10+ (code and CI/test suites written for Python 3.10 or 3.11).
rubric.note: Prompt says Python; skill.md says python/pip are available but does not fix a version. Builder will pick a modern supported Python (3.10/3.11).

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the PyMongo driver (pymongo) compatible with MongoDB 7.0; pin to a recent stable release, e.g. pymongo>=4.3,<5.0.
rubric.note: Prompt asks for a DocumentDB aggregation tool but doesn't name the Python MongoDB driver or version.
skill.md provides cluster details: compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, vector-capable with DiskANN/HNSW/IVF, and the DATABASE name sample_healthcare_11.
skill.md instructs the connection string is in DOCUMENTDB_URI and must not be written into files; use .env.example for placeholders.

rubric.found_in_prompt: based on age, diagnosis, and last-visit documents
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a 'patients' collection with documents containing _id, dob or age, diagnoses (array), and last_visit_date; optionally a 'visits' collection linking patient_id to visit_date if separate visit docs are preferred.
rubric.note: Prompt names the required fields but not collection names, document shapes, relationships, or whether last-visit is embedded or a separate collection.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include a seeded synthetic dataset loader (seed script) that inserts a small set of representative patient and visit documents (dozens to a few hundred) and is idempotent.
rubric.note: Prompt asks for pipeline behavior but provides no sample data or source; skill.md expects the sample to 'load the sample data' during verification but does not supply it.

rubric.found_in_prompt: DocumentDB aggregation tool that identifies patients missing recommended screenings
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement a MongoDB aggregation pipeline ($match on age/diagnosis, $lookup or grouping to find last_visit, $project to compute elapsed interval and compare to guideline thresholds). Create indexes on patients._id, patients.diagnoses, and last_visit_date (or visits.patient_id + visit_date) for performance. Vector indexes mentioned in skill.md are present but vector-dimensions/providers not specified.
rubric.note: The functional query is requested; index definitions and parameters are not specified. skill.md mentions vector indexes exist but doesn't give field names or dimensions relevant to this sample.

rubric.found_in_prompt: LangChain agent...prioritise the patient list and generate outreach talking points
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use an OpenAI-compatible chat model via LangChain (e.g. gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4) for prioritisation and content generation; if embeddings are used for any retrieval, use a text-embedding-3-small style model and set vector-dimension to match that model (e.g. 1536 or as documented). Credentials come from environment variables (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY).
rubric.note: No provider, model names, or embedding model/dimensions/where called are specified.

rubric.found_in_prompt: build a Python LangChain agent ... have the agent prioritise the patient list and generate outreach talking points
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a CLI/demo script (e.g. python run_pipeline.py) that runs the agent end-to-end and prints or writes an ordered patient list with priority and talking points. Optionally include a Jupyter notebook for interactive exploration.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't specify CLI, API, or UI; a simple CLI demo is the least-surprising default.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provision new Azure resources; use the existing cluster per skill.md. No infra-as-code will be provided unless requested.
rubric.note: skill.md forbids creating a new cluster unless policy allows; the prompt doesn't ask for infra as code.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include a README with commands to create a virtualenv, pip install -r requirements.txt, run the seed script, and run the demo CLI. Unit tests may be minimal and not require a live cluster unless explicitly provided.
rubric.note: skill.md gives environment constraints but no explicit run/test commands.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Definition of done: sample runs end-to-end against the provided cluster, creates required collections/indexes idempotently, returns an ordered list of patients with priority and talking points, and includes a README and .env.example.
rubric.note: Prompt does not provide acceptance criteria.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Keep the sample read-only for patient data (no destructive writes), avoid provisioning cloud infra, and keep sample dataset small to limit cost and privacy exposure.
rubric.note: No cost limits, privacy constraints, or non-goals were provided except the skill.md guidance about not writing the connection string.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a conventional layout (src/, tests/, scripts/, README.md); include a pinned requirements.txt; include a .env.example with DOCUMENTDB_URI and any model keys.
rubric.note: skill.md instructs to use a .env.example and not to log secrets; other repo conventions (pinning deps, test structure) are not specified.

contradictions: Starter prompt: "Using the DocumentDB skill" but installed_skills lists no 'DocumentDB' or related agent skill. (There is no installed skill by that name to call.)
skill.md requires use of an existing live cluster and says 'verify against the live cluster' but the prompt's invocation of a 'DocumentDB skill' implies a callable tool that is not installed.
questions_for_author: Which LLM provider and model should the sample use for prioritisation and talking-point generation (e.g. OpenAI gpt-4/gpt-4o-mini)? This affects SDKs, env var names and dimensions if embeddings are used.
Do you want a CLI demo (single script), an HTTP API, or a small web UI? This changes the app surface and what routes/commands to include.
Should the repository include a synthetic seed dataset and an idempotent seed script? If so, any desired size/variety (dozens, hundreds of patients)?
Do you require infrastructure-as-code (Bicep/Terraform) to be included, or must the sample avoid provisioning resources entirely and rely on the provided cluster?
requirements_at_risk: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository. Reason: prompt/skill.md give DOCUMENTDB_URI but do not specify model credential env var names or other model-related settings.

A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values. Reason: skill.md suggests using .env.example for the connection string, but does not enumerate all required env vars (LLM keys, model names, etc.).

The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output. Reason: prompt doesn't name an embedding model nor dimensions; skill.md mentions vector indexes exist but not dimensions tied to a model.
The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them. Reason: neither prompt nor skill.md specify index parameters or guidance.
One database client is created and reused across requests. Reason: not specified; builder may or may not implement a singleton client pattern.

A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data. Reason: prompt doesn't request a seed script; skill.md asks to 'load the sample data' during verification but does not provide a seed script or idempotency requirement explicitly.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails. Reason: prompt does not define an HTTP endpoint or search route; requirement appears out of scope for this prompt.
Search results include the similarity score. Reason: no search API is specified in the prompt; similarity scoring and presentation are unspecified.
Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt. Reason: not mentioned; builder may or may not pin exact versions.
Unit tests run without a live cluster. Reason: prompt does not request unit tests; skill.md expects verification against the live cluster but provides no guidance for offline tests.

Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type. Reason: skill.md explicitly provides an existing cluster and forbids creating another unless allowed; prompt doesn't request infra-as-code.

The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up. Reason: prompt asks for the sample but doesn't require a README; skill.md expects verification but doesn't state README content.

The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name. Reason: prompt uses 'DocumentDB' and references a 'DocumentDB skill' but does not insist on naming conventions; builder might use other product names unless instructed.
